Done. Delivered `effect_gouraud_shaded_cube_ollama-qwen3.8-flash-next-125b-a6b-q4_01.html` (355 lines) — a single self-contained file, Canvas 2D only, no WebGL, no external libraries (verified: zero `src=`/`href=` references).

**Implemented pipeline:**
- **Vertices & topology** — 8 cube corners, 6 quad faces split into 12 triangles (2 per face), plus a deduplicated edge list for the wireframe.
- **Rotation matrices** — full 3×3 `Rz·Ry·Rx` matrix applied per frame on all three axes.
- **Perspective projection** — camera at z=+5, divide-by-depth projection to screen space, near-plane clipping guard.
- **Backface culling** — screen-space signed-area test, validated headless against an independent world-space `normal·viewDir` test over 1000 random orientations (0 disagreements).
- **Gouraud shading** — per-vertex Lambert lighting (`max(0, n·l)` + ambient), then a software triangle rasterizer writing into an `ImageData`/`Uint32Array` framebuffer with barycentric color interpolation (perspective-correct weights) and a z-buffer for occlusion. A headless render confirmed full coverage (15,251 px, no seams/holes) and correct NdotL values.
- **Moving light** — orbits the cube on a tilted path; its position is drawn as a glowing marker projected through the same pipeline.
- **Controls** — `W` toggles the wireframe overlay, `P` pauses/resumes.
- **FPS** — smoothed HUD (top-left) showing FPS, triangle count, and toggle states.

The file passes a Node syntax check of the inline script and all numerical pipeline invariants; open it in any browser to see the rotating, Gouraud-shaded cube.
